items.title: Factor the actual precision as a positive square

source.anchor: Appendix B.2.1 proof of Lemma B.6, equations16-18 and the intervening determinant-sign paragraph
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. ASTIS mathematical restatement.

items.statement: For every natural n>=3, real kappa>=4 and real orthogonal n by n matrix O, put M=(sqrt(kappa)+1)I-(sqrt(kappa)-1)O. The literal precision A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T) equals (1/4) M^T M.
assumptions: n is a natural number with n>=3, retaining the source standing block range.
O belongs to the full real orthogonal group O(n); determinant -1 and +1 are both included.
All square roots are the nonnegative real square root. No Haar law, probabilistic average or integrability premise is part of these pointwise identities.

obligations.label: Factor the actual precision as a positive square

bindings.boundary: Pointwise equations16-18 only. Haar probability and signed averaging, reflection/principal-minor cancellation and equation15, actual Gaussian laws/densities and Fubini, spherical Poisson identities, testing amplification, oracle indistinguishability, and both main lower bounds remain open.

assumption_deltas.source: n>=3,kappa>=4 and an arbitrary real orthogonal O; the positive determinant branch is proved in the source.
assumption_deltas.lean: Exactly these binders; positivity, invertibility and all estimates are derived inside the proof.
assumption_deltas.reason: No convenience premise or restriction to SO(n) is introduced. The continuous path is represented on the same real interval; its nonsingularity uses squared norms rather than a separately stated reverse-triangle lower bound.

items.title: Fix the positive branch of the determinant square root

source.anchor: Appendix B.2.1 proof of Lemma B.6, equations16-18 and the intervening determinant-sign paragraph
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. ASTIS mathematical restatement.

items.statement: For every natural n>=3, real kappa>=4 and real orthogonal n by n matrix O, the nonnegative real square root of det(A_O) equals 2^(-n) det((sqrt(kappa)+1)I-(sqrt(kappa)-1)O). The determinant on the right is positive; it is not replaced by an assumed absolute-value identity.
assumptions: n is a natural number with n>=3, retaining the source standing block range.
O belongs to the full real orthogonal group O(n); determinant -1 and +1 are both included.
All square roots are the nonnegative real square root. No Haar law, probabilistic average or integrability premise is part of these pointwise identities.

items.statement: For every natural n>=3, real kappa>=4 and real orthogonal n by n matrix O of either determinant sign, det(O) sqrt(det(A_O)) equals 2^(-n) det((sqrt(kappa)+1)O-(sqrt(kappa)-1)I).
assumptions: n is a natural number with n>=3, retaining the source standing block range.
O belongs to the full real orthogonal group O(n); determinant -1 and +1 are both included.
